briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon/evening. We will now begin the climate briefing for August 19, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and Global Impacts
sections.content: International news reported today warns of the deepening global threat posed by climate change. Unprecedented marine heatwaves and rising sea temperatures have been observed in European waters, with some parts of the Mediterranean recording temperatures 6°C higher than average [48, 51, 55, 63, 64, 65, 66]. These climate changes are projected to cost London up to £36 billion annually by the 2050s [39], and a study has also revealed that the threat of heatwaves to the aging population is being underestimated [54]. Low water levels due to drought and glacier melt are leading to shocking situations, including the discovery of human remains [56, 71]. In Africa, climate change is severely impacting public health by reshaping the prevalence of diarrheal diseases and epidemic maps, and extending mosquito seasons [44, 67, 68]. Domestically, it has been argued that Seoul's disaster response system requires a fundamental paradigm shift to adapt to the climate crisis [6].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Agricultural and Water Resource Innovation for Climate Change Response
sections.content: In the domestic agricultural sector, facing the direct impacts of climate change, active adaptation efforts are ongoing. Potato farmers in the Seosan region are receiving training on 'survival cultivation methods' to cope with climate change [1], and the Daejeon Agricultural Technology Center is conducting advanced field trips to strengthen young farmers' capacity to respond to climate change [2]. Jangsu County and Sangju City are working to discover new apple varieties and improve the apple industry's resilience in response to climate change [3, 5]. Meanwhile, Korea Water Resources Corporation (K-water) is collaborating with the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) to launch global climate cooperation projects, thereby expanding its climate change response efforts internationally [4].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Accelerating Domestic Efforts for Transition to a Carbon-Neutral Society
sections.content: Various local governments and institutions across the country are accelerating diverse efforts for the transition to a carbon-neutral society. Dobong-gu is pushing forward with a comprehensive 'Climate Justice and Carbon Neutrality' plan, dedicating full efforts to resolve climate inequality [10, 20]. Sejong City is creating a virtuous cycle of carbon neutrality by recycling waste electric wires and eco-bags [11]. Jincheon County is focusing on a carbon-neutral transportation environment, while Yeosu City is allocating supplementary budgets to urban environment improvement and carbon neutrality projects [12, 14, 15]. The Yongin Special City Council is preparing a policy debate to explore circular economy-based carbon-neutral solutions [13, 21]. Hana Financial Group is launching a campaign for employees and customers to practice carbon neutrality in daily life together [16, 23, 26]. The Cheonan Carbon Neutrality Support Center is operating the second phase of its Carbon Neutrality Lifestyle Practice Group [17, 19, 24, 25], thereby raising awareness and encouraging carbon-neutral practices throughout the local community [9, 18, 22]. Furthermore, efforts to solve carbon neutrality challenges and AI power shortages through the development of a Korean artificial sun are also gaining attention [7].

sections.title: ⚠️ Expansion of Renewable Energy and Policy Challenges
sections.content: The expansion of renewable energy is emerging as a crucial agenda both domestically and internationally. Siheung City is supplying customized renewable energy to public facilities, expecting operational cost savings [29, 30], and the rapid growth of the Energy Storage System (ESS) market is driving the expansion of renewable energy [36]. Naver plans to invest in renewable energy power plants in preparation for increased electricity consumption [32], and Haenam County is promoting a 400MW solar power project, establishing 'Haenam-type renewable energy management' [33]. However, there are areas requiring policy and social discussion, such as the controversy surrounding remarks about 'solar farming' [31] and the need for a grace period for the soft landing of domestically produced solar cells [35]. Furthermore, the situation in the combined utility and renewable energy sectors where prices remain stable despite electricity supply shortages [28], and a national research institute's diagnosis of apartment power outages occurring despite electricity surplus [37], suggest that additional efforts are needed for a stable energy transition [76].

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Awareness and Discussions on Climate Change Response
sections.content: In the international community, discussions are underway to raise awareness of climate change and explore various response measures. Talking about climate change has been suggested as one method of response [41], and research has also been published indicating that trading energy stocks can transform skeptics into climate action supporters [45]. Discussions are also active regarding the possibility and risks of responding to climate change through atmospheric manipulation, and who will make decisions on this [42]. Some politicians have caused controversy by revealing a complacent understanding of the climate change crisis [72, 73]. Meanwhile, academic efforts are also being pursued to more systematically analyze and respond to the impacts of climate change, such as the development of a climate impact classification system that operationalizes IPCC's physical drivers and risk concepts [46, 47, 49, 50, 62].

briefing.closing: This concludes today's climate briefing for August 19, 2026. Thank you.
